subject: Proposal: escrowed ramp credits + annual reserve with SLA milestones
messages:
From: Emma Lin <emma.lin@brightlayer.io>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: BrightLayer Procurement <procurement@brightlayer.io>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring move to annual reserve - cashflow & ramp concerns

Sean —

We're evaluating moving BrightLayer from monthly billing to an annual reserve model for 2027 to simplify forecasting. Two concerns from finance: (1) our CFO wants better protection if usage ramps slower than projected (we don't want to prepay for capacity we won't use in Q1), and (2) procurement needs a near-term cashflow smoothing option.

Can Redwood propose structures that give us a meaningful term discount while providing a safety valve for the ramp? We're open to staged invoicing, credits, or an escrow mechanism, but we'll need clear SLA/usage milestones tied to any credit release.

Happy to set up a call this week — copying procurement.

Thanks,
Emma Lin
VP, Finance
BrightLayer

Attachment: (none)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Lin <emma.lin@brightlayer.io>
Cc: BrightLayer Procurement <procurement@brightlayer.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring move to annual reserve - cashflow & ramp concerns

Emma — thanks for the clear ask. Below is a practical proposal that aims to balance BrightLayer's forecasting needs with Redwood's discounting cadence. High level: we can offer an annual reserve with an escrowed ramp-credit pool plus staged invoices so you don't prepay the entire 12 months up front. Key points: 

- Term and list discounting: 12-month term with a year-1 effective discount off list of 18% for the committed reserve. Optional year-2 extension can lock at an additional 2% off after meeting ramp milestones.
- Escrowed ramp credits: We set aside up to 30% of the first-year reserve value as "ramp credits" held in escrow. If BrightLayer does not reach agreed utilization milestones by quarter milestones (Q1/Q2), remaining escrowed funds convert to credits on the account to be consumed or refunded per the table below.
- Staged invoicing: 50% invoiced at signature, 25% at 90 days, 25% at 180 days — each invoice posts as a credit balance against the reserve so you don't physically send all cash up front unless you prefer. We can also offer a 6-invoice monthly amortization if cashflow smoothing is required.
- SLA milestones: quarterly usage thresholds tied to token/throughput baselines. Missed milestones trigger additional credits (up to the escrow amount) and service credits for SLA misses.
- True-up flexibility: allow quarterly true-ups to avoid over-commit risk. True-ups reduce next invoice or refund proportional unused committed capacity.

I've attached an estimates workbook showing sample math at three ramp scenarios (fast / expected / slow) and a draft SOW with milestone language. If this direction looks acceptable, we'll run legal on a short escrow schedule and get finance aligned.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm target committed $ amount or % of current annual run-rate you want to reserve.
2) Choose invoice cadence (3-stage vs 6-month amortization).
3) Approve escrow & milestone framework so we can produce contract language.

I'll set up a quick call with Marissa and Karthik to align on commercial guardrails.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: estimates_v3.xlsx, draft_sow_brightlayer.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: escrowed ramp credits + annual reserve with SLA milestones

Sean — quick internal notes on concession limits and finance asks (copying Karthik/Finance and Lauren/RevOps):

- Escrow mechanism: Finance is OK with an escrow holding as credit on the account rather than a third-party escrow agent — lower ops friction. We should limit refundable cash exposure: escrow cap = 30% first-year reserve, refundable only if BrightLayer terminates without cause in first 180 days. Otherwise unutilized escrow converts to account credits.
- Discounting: legal/finance prefer a maximum of 18% yr1; any extra discount for yr2-extension to be contingent on meeting Q1/Q2 ramp (documented in SOW).
- Invoice cadence: opt for 3-stage invoice by default; if the buyer requires monthly amortization we will need CFO approval per-region (to manage ARR recognition).
- SLA / credits: require objective meter definitions and a maximum service-credit pool cap at 5% of monthly invoice per quarter.

If you want me to push a one-off (higher discount or refundability) I need a deal memo with expected committed value and margin impact.

Marissa
VP, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Lin <emma.lin@brightlayer.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, BrightLayer Procurement <procurement@brightlayer.io>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: escrowed ramp credits + annual reserve with SLA milestones

Emma — following internal alignment, updated approach below (short version):

- Commit: BrightLayer commits to a $600k annual reserve for 12 months (this is a placeholder — we can adjust).
- Discount: 18% effective yr1 discount to list for the committed reserve. Year-2 extension option: additional 2% off if Q1 and Q2 utilization milestones are met.
- Escrow: 30% of yr1 reserve (i.e., $180k) placed as account-held escrow credits. Escrow conversion rules: 
  - If utilization by end of Q2 < 65% of expected, up to 50% of escrow converts immediately to credits you can apply; remainder refunded as account credit schedule or applied to future invoices (not cash refund unless termination).
  - Refund to cash only if BrightLayer terminates for convenience within the first 180 days and requests refund; otherwise balance becomes account credit.
- Invoicing options: 3-stage (50/25/25) or 6-month amortization. You indicated preference for less current cash outflow — propose 6-month amortization on accounting side and Redwood will record revenue per ASC rules.
- SLAs: we will define measurable throughput and latency baselines in SOW. SLA credits capped at 5% monthly per quarter.

Attached: execution_summary.pdf and a draft escrow clause for legal to review. Can you confirm: (A) committed amount you'd like to target, (B) invoice cadence, (C) whether you need cash refunds vs account credits for unused escrow?

If you confirm, I'll generate a short DocuSign with these commercial terms for signature and kick off legal to finalize the escrow language.

Thanks,
Sean
Attachment: execution_summary.pdf, escrow_agreement_draft.docx
From: Emma Lin <emma.lin@brightlayer.io>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: BrightLayer Procurement <procurement@brightlayer.io>, BrightLayer Legal <legal@brightlayer.io>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: escrowed ramp credits + annual reserve with SLA milestones

Sean — appreciate the clarity. BrightLayer is comfortable in principle with the 18% yr1 discount and the escrow-credit construct, but procurement has two asks before we sign: 

1) Soften the ramp milestones slightly — replace the 65% end-Q2 threshold with a graduated schedule (50% at end-Q1, 70% at end-Q2) to reflect our expected seasonality.
2) We need a quarterly true-up option that can reduce committed capacity without penalty (up to 10% of committed amount) if actual usage falls materially below forecast. This will make the CFO comfortable with the annual commitment.

We prefer account credits over cash refunds for simplicity but procurement wants a defined refund path in the rare termination-for-convenience case — suggested language: refund request triggers 60-day review and payments if validated.

If Redwood can accept those two changes, procurement is prepared to issue a PO next week and route the DocuSign. Copying legal for escrow language review.

—Emma

Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: escrowed ramp credits + annual reserve with SLA milestones

Emma — great, we can accept the two changes you requested. Final commercial summary below: 

- Committed reserve (placeholder): $600,000 for 12 months; please confirm PO amount if different.
- Discount: 18% effective off list in yr1. Year-2 optional extension at an additional 2% if quarter milestones are met.
- Escrowed ramp credits: 30% of yr1 reserve ($180k) held as account-credit escrow. Conversion schedule updated per your ask: 50% conversion if utilization >=50% at end-Q1; additional conversion upon >=70% at end-Q2.
- Quarterly true-up: allow reduction up to 10% of committed capacity at quarterly true-up window without penalty; any further reduction subject to pro-rata adjustments.
- Invoice cadence: 6-month amortization (preferred by BrightLayer) — finance will accept with revenue recognition caveat.
- Refund path: account-credit default; cash refund possible only for termination-for-convenience with 60-day validation and approval.
- SLA credits: capped at 5% monthly invoice per quarter; measurable definitions will be added to SOW.

Next steps I will execute today:
1) Produce DocuSign with the commercial summary and attach the draft escrow clause + SOW appendix. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.net/secure/exec?doc=DL-7843
2) Loop legal to finalize escrow_agreement_draft.docx (attached).
3) Expect PO and routing from procurement to close on signature.

Thank you — excited to get this live.

Best,
